readingInstruction: Read 2 John, a single chapter. It is the shortest book in the Bible by Greek word count and takes about two minutes to read. Notice how truth and love are joined, and how hospitality has limits when false teaching is at stake.
settingTheScene: Second John is a personal letter from “the elder” (the apostle John, in his old age) to “the elect lady and her children,” either a local congregation or a Christian woman and her family. The occasion was the same as in 1 John: itinerant teachers who denied that Jesus had come in the flesh were traveling from church to church. In the ancient world, traveling teachers depended on hospitality, and a believer’s home could become a base for false teaching. John writes to praise faithfulness and to give a warning.
observation: “The elect lady and her children, whom I love in truth” (v. 1).
“I rejoiced greatly to find some of your children walking in the truth” (v. 4).
“And this is love, that we walk according to his commandments” (v. 6).
“For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh” (v. 7).
“Watch yourselves, so that you may not lose what we have worked for, but may win a full reward” (v. 8).
“Whoever abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son” (v. 9).
“Do not receive him into your house or give him any greeting” (v. 10).
“So that our joy may be complete” (v. 12).
interpretation:
John greets the church with love “in truth” and with the grace of “truth and love.” The words “truth” and “love” occur together throughout the letter, and both are essential. Truth without love is hard, and love without truth is sentimental. John says that the truth “abides in us and will be with us forever.” He rejoices that some of the children are walking in the truth, just as the Father commanded.

His request is the old commandment: “that we love one another. And this is love, that we walk according to his commandments.” Love is not just a feeling; it is obedience. This is the same message as in 1 John 5:3.

Then the warning: “For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. Such a one is the deceiver and the antichrist.” The false teachers were denying the incarnation. John tells the readers to watch themselves, so as not to lose the fruit of their labors but to receive a full reward. He draws the line sharply: “Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ, does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.” Those who “go on ahead” claim to advance beyond the apostles’ teaching, but in fact they leave Christ behind.

The practical instruction is: “If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house or give him any greeting, for whoever greets him takes part in his wicked works.” How do we apply this? It does not forbid showing kindness to unbelievers or neighbors, and it does not tell us to be rude to those who disagree on secondary matters. It concerns teachers who deny the core of the gospel, particularly the person and work of Christ, and who come as representatives of Christian faith. To welcome and fund such a teacher would be to support his work. Each situation calls for wisdom. We should hold firmly to the truth, and we should treat the people we disagree with with the patience Christ showed.

The letter ends as it began, with warm personal greetings: John hopes to visit and speak face to face, “so that our joy may be complete.” The children of your elect sister greet you. Nothing replaces the presence of Christians together.
connection: 1 John 2:18-27 and 4:1-6 give the same warning. 1 John 5:3 ties love to obedience. John 14:15 and 15:10 are Jesus’ words on keeping his commandments. Galatians 1:6-9 pronounces a curse on a different gospel. Titus 3:10-11 instructs us to avoid a divisive person after warnings. Romans 16:17-18 also tells us to watch out for those who cause divisions. Romans 12:13 and Hebrews 13:2 commend hospitality. Matthew 5:43-48 teaches love for enemies. Ephesians 4:15 speaks of speaking the truth in love.
application:
Memorize verse 6: love is walking according to God’s commandments.

Ask whether you tend to emphasize truth or love, and which you may be neglecting. Take one step to bring them together.

Test what you hear and read about Jesus by the apostolic teaching. If something denies Christ’s deity or humanity, be cautious.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for truth and love in Jesus.
Ask him to help you walk in the truth and love by obeying.
Ask him to keep you from deceivers.
